questions.question: The "Linguine Sign" on MRI is diagnostic for which condition?
questions.detail: The "linguine" represents the collapsed elastomer shell floating within the silicone gel.

questions.question: Which sign describes silicone gel outside of both the elastomer shell AND the fibrous capsule?
choices: Snowstorm sign (on ultrasound) or extracapsular globules (on MRI/CT)
questions.detail: Silicone in the axillary lymph nodes or breast tissue indicates extracapsular rupture.

questions.question: The "Keyhole" or "Noose" sign on MRI refers to:
choices: Silicone trapped between the shell and the fibrous capsule (intracapsular rupture)
questions.detail: This is a sign of an uncollapsed intracapsular rupture.

questions.question: "Saline" implant rupture is usually diagnosed by:
choices: Clinical exam (the breast deflates rapidly) and mammography
questions.detail: When saline leaks, the fluid is absorbed and the implant volume is lost.

questions.question: After a lumpectomy, the "surgical bed" typically appears as:
choices: An area of architectural distortion with a fluid collection (seroma) that evolves into a scar
questions.detail: The appearance changes over time, often resolving into a stable scar.

questions.question: "Fat Necrosis" is a common sequela of breast surgery. Which finding is MOST helpful to avoid an unnecessary biopsy?
choices: Internal macroscopic fat (radiolucent center) on mammography
questions.detail: Fat is the only substance in the breast that is darker than water-density cancer on a mammogram.

questions.question: A "Capsular Contracture" is a complication of implants where:
choices: The fibrous capsule thickens and tightens, distorting the breast
The implant turns into a cancer
questions.detail: This is a clinical diagnosis but appears on imaging as a rounded, "balled-up" implant.

questions.question: Mammographic "Eklund" (Implant-Displaced) views are used to:
choices: Better visualize the native breast tissue by pushing the implant posteriorly
Compress the implant to its limit
questions.detail: Standard views are often obscured by the radiopaque implant.

questions.question: "Biopsy clips" are placed during a procedure to:
choices: Mark the site for future surgical localization or to confirm the area was sampled
questions.detail: Clips are essential for "radiology-pathology correlation" and future follow-up.

questions.question: "Specimen Radiography" is performed during surgery to:
choices: Confirm that the targeted suspicious calcifications or mass are within the excised tissue
questions.detail: This ensures the surgeon has accurately sampled the lesion identified by the radiologist.
